description: Address sequencer holding 100 editable sixteen-step patterns, each step a number from 1 to 16 put out as a voltage

params.text: Sets the address this step of the pattern points at, by clicking one of the sixteen cells in its column; the row marked 1 is address zero
Gives every step that is not held a new random number, between the Rnd Min and Rnd Max set in the menu
Sets how many steps are played before the pattern starts again, 2 to 16
Shifts where in the pattern the playing starts, 0 to 15 steps
Sets the address space the step numbers are spread over, 2 to 32; use 16 to address TD4
Picks which of the 100 patterns is played and edited
Copies the sixteen step numbers of the current pattern
Writes the copied step numbers into the current pattern
While on, the pattern is picked by hand and a cable in the pattern input no longer moves the selection
While on, a randomise leaves this step of the pattern untouched
Turns the current pattern back to front, so its sixteen step numbers run in the opposite order

inputs.text: Each rising edge moves on to the next step of the pattern
A rising edge returns to the first step and blocks the clock for 1ms
Selects the pattern, 0.1V per pattern over 0-10V; while it is patched the pattern cannot be picked by hand unless Lock is on
A trigger gives every step that is not held a new random number, between the Rnd Min and Rnd Max set in the menu
Sets the offset, 1.6 steps per volt over 0-10V, and overrides the Offset knob while patched

outputs.text: The step number the pattern has reached, as a voltage: the step number divided by the size, times 10
All sixteen step numbers of the current pattern at once, one per channel, with as many channels as the Length knob sets

menu: DivBy10 — divides both outputs by ten, so a size of 16 gives 0.0625V per step in place of 0.625V
Insert Pattern — pushes the patterns after the current one along by one place and empties the current one; the hundredth pattern is lost
Delete Pattern — removes the current pattern and pulls every later pattern back one place
Rnd Min — sets the lowest step number a randomise can write, 0 to 15
Rnd Max — sets the highest step number a randomise can write, 0 to 15

inputs.0: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.2: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.4: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
